lead.t: Understanding replication is essential for understanding pathogenesis — viral replication causes cell damage and death — and for understanding antiviral drug targets, since most antivirals work by blocking specific steps in replication.
lead.s: EXAM: Basic Virology, Viral Replication, Prions & Slow Viruses — Past Paper

b: Antivirals target specific stages of the viral replication cycle:
Entry/Fusion Inhibitors : Block viral attachment to host cells or fusion of the viral envelope with the host membrane (e.g., Enfuvirtide for HIV, Maraviroc for HIV).
Uncoating Inhibitors : Prevent the release of the viral genome into the host cytoplasm (e.g., Amantadine for Influenza A, though resistance is common).

Nucleoside/Nucleotide Analogues : Mimic natural nucleosides/nucleotides, getting incorporated into the viral DNA/RNA during replication and terminating chain elongation or inhibiting viral polymerases. Examples include Acyclovir (HSV, VZV),
Protease Inhibitors : Block viral proteases, which are essential for cleaving viral polyproteins into functional individual proteins required for viral assembly (e.g., Saquinavir for HIV).

qs.q: Which class of antiviral drugs specifically targets and blocks the integration of viral genetic material into the host cell genome?
qs.e: Integrase inhibitors block the integration of viral DNA into the host genome. Protease inhibitors block viral maturation instead of genome integration.

qs.q: Which antiviral drug is used as post-exposure prophylaxis for HIV?
qs.e: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for HIV uses a three-drug regimen, typically tenofovir/emtricitabine (NRTIs) plus dolutegravir (INSTI). It must be initiated within 72 hours of exposure and continued for 28 days. This combination is highly effective at preventing HIV transmission.

qs.q: Many antiviral drugs act by inhibition of a viral DNA polymerase enzyme. Select the virus for which this class of drugs would be effective.
qs.e: CMV is a DNA virus that uses its own DNA polymerase for replication, making it a valid target for DNA polymerase inhibitors like ganciclovir. Influenza, measles, and mumps are RNA viruses.
